text: And not every year for 20 or 30 years. We about to fact check this sh**. Well, just when I was ready to move on from this whole story, SimpleBlackTheory showed openly what kind of person he is. After getting so much love from his own viewers, he first apologized in his comment section. Then he came to my channel and wrote that I was right and that he makes things up. I was satisfied with that. I was ready to turn the page. But right after that, he suddenly forgot all of it. He DMs me saying he wants a live debate, which I told him I'm not interested in. Then he starts calling me a fraud, says that he tore my video to shreds, puts our private, I repeat, private communication in his story without asking my permission, and keeps asking me to break down his answer. Even though he was reacting to my video, so it was his job to break down my arguments, not mix them up, not switch them around, and not avoid the strongest points. Anyways, I don't think I need to tell you how disappointed I am in this guy. At this point, I'm not interested in having any kind of deal with him. Because as Warren Buffett once said, you can't make a good deal with a bad person. I may still react to some of his videos if I find them interesting enough, but at this point, I am just really disappointed. Still, even though he pretty much ignored or straight up switched my points, and even though he was supposed to be fact-checking me, I decided why not to take a look at his last video reacting to me. Once again, despite his behavior, I will try to be objective. First, the reason why I'm continuing this conversation is because the idea that being pregnant is not a more dangerous job than being a police is a dangerous idea. I mean, statistically, more people die in maternal death than police officers die in the line of duty. In 2024, 649 people lost their life from maternal death, while only 149 officers lost their lives in 2024. Seriously, you are comparing absolute numbers, not per capita? Adjusting for the size of the group is one of the most basic principles in statistics. And this confuses me because in his other videos, he was working with divisions, even though he used percentages in a wrong way. Like guys, how do you seriously expect me to react to someone who uses absolute numbers to support a claim about risk? For example, the CDC says that over 4,000 unintentional drowning deaths occur in the US every year. The NSC says that 5,553 people died from choking in 2022. So by his logic, if we use absolute numbers, swimming pools, bathtubs, and eating dinner are more than six times more dangerous than being pregnant and around 26 times more dangerous than being a cop? Does that sound serious to you? Later in the video, he talks about poverty-stricken or disadvantaged women having higher risks during pregnancy. And yes, that is a fair point. Pregnancy risks are not the same for everyone. They vary by income, health care access, race, age, medical conditions, and many other factors. But the question is, how is that related to the claim that being pregnant is more dangerous than being a cop? Look, guys, the risks associated with pregnancy are real. It should be talked about. And it is an important topic to raise awareness about. But why mix it with a completely unrelated comparison? How are cops even relevant to this? Also, let me show you this moment. In fact, we've seen in 2023 that 98% of maternal death came from low or lower middle income countries. So the statistic says 92%. In the video, he says 98%. Then while editing, he apparently realizes he made a mistake and corrects it with an asterisk to 93%. What a joke. And with this, I want to finish this topic. Once again, for me, this guy is just a dishonest disappointment.
